owner_questions[1].title.en: Do we arm the watchdog, and in which mode?

owner_questions[1].context.en: CALIBRATION CORRECTION: installing it is YOUR step by design — runbook GSL-57 marks the launchctl commands as “performed by the OWNER”. The engineering side is finished: code, 75 green tests, a runbook. It has been waiting fourteen days.

owner_questions[1].why_recommended.en: An observation-only run gives data without risk, and the very first tick will show whether the audit was right about the session name and the thresholds. The third option is not enough: the platform supervisor cannot be installed as a service and dies with the last client — verified on this machine.

owner_questions[1].sub_fork.en: Patch the current watchdog (watchdog.conf + a reality gate) or narrow it onto the platform (liveness sourced from claude agents --json). I recommend narrowing it: the part that turned out to be misconfigured is precisely the home-made process handling.

owner_questions[1].options[0].label.en: An observation-only run for a few days: it ticks, it writes a ledger, kill and re-wake are disabled

owner_questions[1].options[1].label.en: Arm it immediately after the reality gate

owner_questions[1].options[2].label.en: Do not arm it; rely on the platform supervisor

owner_questions[2].title.en: Who edits the skills now, and how?

owner_questions[2].context.en: The loop “lesson → skill edit” ran for 30 days and stopped on 10 July; the guard placed on install.sh on 20 July froze that stop in place by removing the only documented synchronisation path. Formally the global copy is authoritative — but it sits outside git, outside review, outside Jira, and nobody edits it. Because of that, the mandate's central deliverable stopped developing.

owner_questions[2].why_recommended.en: The audit showed that five of six skills are BYTE-IDENTICAL, so the guard's original justification (“the local copy has problems”) is not substantively supported. But the guard is still needed — for a different reason: install.sh syncs local→global across ALL subfolders at once, and a single run today would roll back the ATLASSIAN_API_TOKEN lesson in using-jira. The recommended option keeps the protection and restores a controlled path. This is the root cause that survived calibration completely.

owner_questions[2].sub_fork.en: Whether to allow a one-off reverse sync of the tmux-agents-orchestration skill from ~/.claude/skills/ into the repository. Today it is not in git at all. I recommend allowing it.

owner_questions[2].options[0].label.en: You sanction edits to the global copy through a GSL task with review, then a targeted rsync global→local to record it in git; the guard stays

owner_questions[2].options[1].label.en: Return authority to the skill/ folder and enable install.sh for explicitly named skills

owner_questions[3].title.en: Agent permissions: leave them off, enumerate them, or relay them through Channels?

owner_questions[3].context.en: There is no permissions block in .claude/settings.json at all. The orchestrator runs as claude --dangerously-skip-permissions. The problem “a permission prompt ends the night” is already solved — by there being no permissions left: an autonomous LLM at night holds an unrestricted shell on a personal machine, together with gh, the Jira MCP, subscription keys in the keychain and write access to the shared tree; meanwhile agents browse the web and start third-party MCP servers. No report called this a decision — it simply happened.

owner_questions[3].channels_nuance.en: Channels give two different things, and they must be kept apart. Pushing events into a live session is close to what you froze (mobile and notifications). Permission relay is NOT a mobile feature, it is an autonomy mechanism: “Channel servers that declare the permission relay capability can forward these prompts to you so you can approve or deny remotely”. A permission prompt at 3 a.m. stops ending the night. The price is a mirror image of today's risk: “Anyone who can reply through the channel can approve or deny tool use in your session, so only allowlist senders you trust”. Today the risk is that the agent approves everything itself; with relay the risk is that everything is approved by whoever holds the Telegram account. Plus one limit: “Events only arrive while the session is open” — relay complements a supervisor, it does not replace one.

owner_questions[3].why_recommended.en: An enumerated allowlist covers 95 percent of cases, costs nothing at night and adds no new trust surface. Relay solves the remaining 5 percent, but only makes sense once the 95 are enumerated — otherwise it turns into a permanent watch beside the phone. And separately: switching on a Telegram channel now would reverse your push-freeze directive without asking, which is why this is posed as a question rather than decided.

owner_questions[3].options[0].label.en: Enumerate permissions explicitly: inventory what agents actually call, write permissions.allow, drop --dangerously-skip-permissions

owner_questions[3].options[1].label.en: Enumerate, plus Channels with relay for the remainder

owner_questions[3].options[2].label.en: Leave it as it is — fastest for autonomy, an unrestricted shell at night

owner_questions[4].title.en: What number do we set as the token ceiling?

owner_questions[4].context.en: This is the ONLY missing input for the main indicator — calibration showed that the second supposed input (polling the tracker) does not affect the answer by construction: the “work” axis is declared on_exhaustion:completes and is not part of the set of stopping clocks. And the absence of a ceiling is a state your own manifest explicitly provides for, in section 5.phase-ceiling.

owner_questions[4].why_recommended.en: Any number beats a missing one: today the mechanism cannot be wrong only because it cannot fire.

owner_questions[4].options[0].label.en: One number per night in GOSLEEP_TOKEN_CEILING, taken from observed spend (a cumulative ~16 million tokens over 98 cycles), revisited in a week

owner_questions[4].options[2].label.en: A dollar ceiling via --max-budget-usd for the -p glue

owner_questions[5].title.en: What carries the external tick: launchd or Claude Desktop scheduled tasks?

owner_questions[5].context.en: launchd survives a reboot, but StartInterval does not tick while the machine sleeps; tonight's wakefulness currently rests on a manually started caffeinate, with the system set to sleep after 1 minute. Desktop scheduled tasks offer a 1-minute minimum, a catch-up run after wake, learnable permissions and a history with reasons for skips — but they require the app to be running and have never been tested on this account.

owner_questions[5].why_recommended.en: Neither of the two survives the machine being switched off — that is a platform limit, not ours; so the choice has to be made on observed night-time behaviour, not on documentation.

owner_questions[5].options[0].label.en: Pre-flight both; the primary is whichever survives real nights; launchd as the fallback

owner_questions[6].title.en: Do we unfreeze the second version of the web interface?

owner_questions[6].context.en: The PRD deliberately deferred the interactive dashboard (server, SSE, a narrow action list) as v2, annotated “Not an orphan — a deliberate defer”. Your directive of 24 July about “all features and all services” could THEORETICALLY unfreeze it — but that is a scope decision, not a defect, and it would be wrong to take it on your behalf. Worth knowing: the mandate's web paragraph (line 13) asks only for indicators and observation; the phrase “so that it can be orchestrated” comes from the mobile paragraph (line 17), which you froze. So unfreezing v2 extends the mandate rather than fulfilling it.

owner_questions[6].why_recommended.en: It delivers the most within days and closes nothing off: if you decide to unfreeze v2, the finding returns to the plan intact, with an inventory of write paths already prepared.

owner_questions[6].options[0].label.en: Keep the web as a v1 display: bring freshness, connectedness and quality to a professional level (epic 4); control stays in the terminal

owner_questions[6].options[1].label.en: Unfreeze v2 now: a server on 127.0.0.1, live data, a narrow explicit action list strictly through lab-emit (the write path is already written)

owner_questions[6].options[2].label.en: v2 after the first controlled night

owner_questions[7].title.en: When do we run the first real night?

owner_questions[7].context.en: The system has NEVER ONCE run during the hours it is named after: 18 events between 03:00 and 06:00 across seven days of logs. All three record autonomy windows were working evenings with the owner awake.

owner_questions[7].why_recommended.en: The tick makes the night self-documenting even if the orchestrator dies. Without a controlled night, any claim about autonomy stays an extrapolation from evenings.

owner_questions[7].options[0].label.en: One controlled night immediately after epic 3, with a fixed task and a known set of forks

owner_questions[7].options[1].label.en: After epic 5 (once the watchdog is armed)
